# The moment I overruled the machine

Nine hours into the build, I stopped and asked a question I should have asked first. The answer invalidated two claims the whole repo was resting on. This is the single most important thing in this submission.

---

## "Do you know what the task was?"

`2026-07-09T22:17:57.350Z` · session `ba66928b` · branch `fleek-influencer-deck-drafts-353c7d`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> I need to approach this differently. If we look at the task in hand, do you have the job description and the influencer marketing engine task and case study task at hand? Do Do you have it in mind? Do you know what the task was?

**What came back:**

> Honest answer first: I have the **Draft 2 approach doc** (the six-section plan we've been executing), but I haven't read the **original task brief or the job description verbatim** this session — I only know them second-hand through references ("same six-section chronology as the task brief", "activation % is Fleek's own JD headline metric"). Let me check whether they live in the repo before I claim anything.

**What changed because of it:** Nine hours of building on a paraphrase. I stopped everything and asked whether the model had ever actually read the job description and the case-study brief. It had not — nobody had put them in the repo. Everything downstream of this question changed.

## The constants had no source of truth

`2026-07-09T22:26:27.362Z` · session `02aedcaf` · branch `main`

**The engine put a decision to Doug, and he answered:**

> **Q.** The JD and task brief don't exist as files anywhere in this repo — they're only paraphrased inside docs/01 and docs/04. That's the core structural flaw: the constants have no source of truth. How do you want to land them?
>
> **A.** Scaffold now, you paste after (Recommended)
>
> **Q.** The brain folder got renamed on disk (FLEEK BRAIN → "Fleek Knowledge Base") but not in git, so git sees 24 deletions and the agent definition still points at the old path. What should the folder be called?
>
> **A.** Fleek wiki
>

**What changed because of it:** Confirmed: the JD and task brief existed nowhere as files. They had been paraphrased into two docs, and the paraphrase had drifted. We scaffolded `mission/` for the real documents and made it read-only to agents.

## Supplying the source documents

`2026-07-09T23:03:30.744Z` · session `02aedcaf` · branch `repo-architecture`

**What Doug typed, verbatim:**

> @"~/Downloads/influencer_specialist _casestudy.pdf" @"~/Downloads/JD_influencer_marketing_manager.pdf" @"~/Downloads/fleek_task_draft_2.docx"
> find here attached the JD, the case study and my draft no.2 plan

**What came back:**

> Both landed. Let me get the remaining pages and the docx.

**What changed because of it:** Reading the real JD against the repo immediately falsified two load-bearing claims. **First:** the wiki asserted "Fleek has no structured creator program — greenfield, not a fix-up." The JD describes a 1,000+ creator roster built over two years with recruitment largely automated. The wiki had inferred absence from Fleek's *public* surface and treated it as absence in fact. Saying "you have no creator program" in the first two minutes of the interview would have been unrecoverable. **Second:** the strategy anchored on activation with recruitment as a footnote; the brief weights both. Both corrections are recorded, dated, at the bottom of `mission/mission.md` — not quietly patched.
